strings.d1.s0.name: Colosseo
strings.d1.s0.tips: One ticket covers the Colosseum, Forum and Palatine (about 18 EUR). Book the 08:30 first slot online. The arena floor costs extra, there is no shade, so bring water.
strings.d1.s1.name: Foro Romano
strings.d1.s1.tips: Included in the same ticket. Walk along the Via Sacra to the Temple of Vesta.
strings.d1.s2.name: Palatino
strings.d1.s2.tips: Imperial palaces and views over the Forum, plus an orange garden.
strings.d1.s3.name: Trattoria Luzzi
strings.d1.s3.tips: A cheap, no-frills local trattoria next to the Colosseum. Try the cacio e pepe; the queue moves fast.
strings.d1.s4.name: Piazza del Campidoglio
strings.d1.s4.tips: Michelangelo's square. The terrace behind it has a free sunset view over the Forum.
strings.d1.b0.name: Li Rioni Pizzeria
strings.d1.b0.tips: Roman-style pizza near the Colosseum, open in the evening.
strings.d1.b1.name: Basilica di San Clemente
strings.d1.b1.tips: A three-level church (built over a Roman temple), right next to the Colosseum.
strings.d2.s0.name: Musei Vaticani
strings.d2.s0.tips: Book the 08:00 first slot for the Sistine Chapel (25 EUR online, 60 days ahead). Expect the Raphael Rooms and long corridors.
strings.d2.s1.name: Basilica di San Pietro
strings.d2.s1.tips: Free, but there is a security queue. The dome costs 10 EUR (551 steps), and the Pietà is by the entrance.
strings.d2.s2.name: Bonci Pizzarium
strings.d2.s2.tips: Gabriele Bonci's pizza by the slice, eaten standing up. Nearest metro: Cipro (Vatican).
strings.d2.s3.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
strings.d2.s3.tips: Hadrian's mausoleum turned fortress, with a terrace view of the Vatican.
strings.d2.s4.name: Ponte Sant'Angelo
strings.d2.s4.tips: Bernini's bridge lined with angels. Take your photos before sunset.
strings.d2.b0.name: Pizzeria Da Remo Testaccio
strings.d2.b0.tips: Thin Roman pizza in Testaccio, open in the evening.
strings.d2.b1.name: Giardini Vaticani
strings.d2.b1.tips: Guided tour of the Vatican Gardens, as an alternative to the castle.
strings.d3.theme: Baroque Rome: Pantheon, Navona and Trevi
strings.d3.s0.name: Pantheon
strings.d3.s0.tips: See the oculus in the dome. Entry is 5 EUR; morning light is best, and there is Mass on Sundays.
strings.d3.s1.name: Piazza Navona
strings.d3.s1.tips: Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers. The cafés are pricey, so come for the photos.
strings.d3.s2.name: Campo de' Fiori
strings.d3.s2.tips: Morning market with cheese, spices and truffle products.
strings.d3.s3.name: Roscioli Salumeria
strings.d3.s3.tips: Carbonara and a deli counter, among the best in Rome. Booking is essential.
strings.d3.s4.name: Trevi Fountain
strings.d3.s4.tips: Toss in a coin. It is empty at 07:00 or 23:00 and packed by day (entry system in place since 2025).
strings.d3.b0.name: Armando al Pantheon
strings.d3.b0.tips: Roman cooking since 1961, next to the Pantheon. Reserve ahead.
strings.d3.b1.name: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
strings.d3.b1.tips: A private palace collection with Caravaggio and Velázquez, a calmer option than Trevi.
strings.d4.s0.name: Santa Maria in Trastevere
strings.d4.s0.tips: One of Rome's oldest churches dedicated to Mary, with golden mosaics. Quiet in the morning.
strings.d4.s1.name: Trastevere Streets
strings.d4.s1.tips: Cobblestones and ivy-covered walls; head along Via della Lungaretta.
strings.d4.s2.name: Da Enzo al 29
strings.d4.s2.tips: A small Trastevere classic serving amatriciana and artichokes. Join the queue when it opens at 12:00.
strings.d4.s3.name: Villa Farnesina
strings.d4.s3.tips: A Renaissance villa with Raphael frescoes. Peaceful.
strings.d4.s4.name: Gianicolo Terrace
strings.d4.s4.tips: Rome's best free view, with the Garibaldi monument. Come at sunset.
strings.d4.b0.name: Trapizzino Trastevere
strings.d4.b0.tips: Stew stuffed into a pizza pocket. Street food.
strings.d4.b1.name: Orto Botanico di Roma
strings.d4.b1.tips: A botanical garden in Trastevere, as an alternative to the villa.
strings.d5.s0.name: Galleria Borghese
strings.d5.s0.tips: Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings in a 2-hour slot. Booking weeks ahead is mandatory.
strings.d5.s1.name: Villa Borghese Gardens
strings.d5.s1.tips: A park walk; from the Pincio terrace you look over Piazza del Popolo.
strings.d5.s2.name: Spanish Steps
strings.d5.s2.tips: No sitting on the steps. Via Condotti is nearby.
strings.d5.s3.name: Pastificio Guerra
strings.d5.s3.tips: Fresh pasta for 5 EUR behind the Spanish Steps. There is a queue at 13:00.
strings.d5.s4.name: Ara Pacis
strings.d5.s4.tips: Augustus's altar of peace, housed in Richard Meier's glass pavilion. Air-conditioned.
strings.d5.b0.name: Ginger Sapori e Salute
strings.d5.b0.tips: A light Italian lunch near Spagna.
strings.d5.b1.name: Piazza del Popolo
strings.d5.b1.tips: Twin churches and a Caravaggio (Santa Maria del Popolo, free).
strings.d6.s0.name: Ostia Antica
strings.d6.s0.tips: 30 minutes from Rome (metro and train). A port city as well preserved as Pompeii, with mosaic-floored baths. There is little shade.
strings.d6.s1.name: Ostia Lido Beach
strings.d6.s1.tips: 10 minutes from the ancient city, this is the Romans' own beach. A stabilimento (private beach club) sunbed costs 10-20 EUR.
strings.d6.s2.name: Ristorante Ostia Lido Balık
strings.d6.s2.tips: Seafood on the beach, best between lunch and dinner.
strings.d6.b0.name: Sbarco di Enea Ostia
strings.d6.b0.tips: A trattoria by the Ostia Antica exit.
strings.d6.b1.name: Frascati
strings.d6.b1.tips: A wine town in the hills outside Rome, as an alternative to Ostia.
strings.d7.s0.name: Mercato Testaccio
strings.d7.s0.tips: A local market. At Mordi e Vai, try the beef stew sandwich and supplì (fried rice balls).
strings.d7.s1.name: Pyramid of Cestius and Non-Catholic Cemetery
strings.d7.s1.tips: A pyramid in Rome and the Keats-Shelley cemetery, with resident cats.
strings.d7.s2.name: Aventine Orange Garden
strings.d7.s2.tips: Giardino degli Aranci and the Knights of Malta keyhole: a farewell view.
strings.d7.s3.name: Flavio al Velavevodetto
strings.d7.s3.tips: A trattoria carved into Monte Testaccio. Order the carbonara and coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew).
strings.d7.s4.name: Roma Termini
strings.d7.s4.tips: The Leonardo Express reaches Fiumicino in 32 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Trapizzino Testaccio
strings.d7.b0.tips: Stew in a pizza pocket, a quick farewell bite.
strings.d7.b1.name: Baths of Caracalla
strings.d7.b1.tips: The vast ruins of a Roman bathhouse, as an alternative to the pyramid.
strings.note0: Rome is walkable. Metro lines A and B are limited; bus 64 goes to the Vatican. The Leonardo Express to Fiumicino costs 14 EUR. The Roma Pass (48 or 72 hours) covers museums and transport.
strings.note1: Timed online tickets are essential for the Colosseum, Vatican Museums and Borghese. Book Borghese weeks ahead and the Vatican 60 days ahead.
strings.note2: Summer reaches 33-38°C: finish the ancient sites by 08:30, spend 13:00-16:00 indoors or in a siesta, and eat dinner after 20:00. Some trattorias close in August for Ferragosto.
strings.note3: Rome's four classic pastas: carbonara, cacio e pepe, amatriciana and gricia. Coperto (cover charge) is 2-3 EUR, and tipping means rounding up.
strings.note4: Cover shoulders and knees in churches (the Vatican is strict). The street fountains (nasoni) give drinkable water, so refill your bottle.
strings.note5: Watch for pickpockets on bus 64 and at Termini. At Trevi and Spagna, say 'no grazie' to bracelet sellers.
